record.site_desc: This site is established within Desert Botanical Gardens founded to conserve desert plants and habitats in a rapidly expanding metropolitan region in Phoenix, Arizona. The site is managed by the Central Arizona Phoenix Long-term Ecological Research (CAP-LTER) program. This flux tower is equipped with CSAT3 and Li-7500 for eddy covariance measurement. According to the USDA Soil Survey Map, the soil type is Cavelt gravelly loam and Rillito gravelly loam. There is close proximity to a water canal, parking lot and turf grass facility toward the east.

grp_location.location_comment: Located in an open metropolitan desert park in Phoenix, Arizona. The tower is located along a slope, with a hill 183 meters to the west, and an open water canal 100 meters on the east, with a parking lot 150 meters aways in the northeast direction (the dominant wind direction).

grp_igbp.igbp_comment: The vegetation consists of Saguaro cactus and patchy coverage of desert shrubs, such as creosote bush (Larrea tridentata).
